title: SMART FINANCE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM BASED ON ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TECHNOLOGIES
venue: Problems of applied mathematics and mathematical modeling
tldr: Integrates k-NN, decision trees, ARIMA, LSTM, Isolation Forests, autoencoders, SVM, and LLMs into a modular personal finance management system achieving 91.2% classification accuracy and 6.8% MAPE for forecasting.
problem_and_motivation: Traditional budgeting methods lack accuracy and adaptability for modern financial data complexity. AI technologies offer potential to transform personal finance management through automated analysis and optimization. Existing systems need integration of multiple AI approaches for comprehensive financial support.
approach: Developed a two-level modular architecture with analytical computation and AI recommendation blocks.
Implemented k-NN and decision trees for transaction categorization using Euclidean distance and information gain.
Used ARIMA and LSTM models for expense forecasting with time series data.
Applied Isolation Forests, autoencoders, and SVM for anomaly detection in transactions.
Integrated matrix factorization and collaborative filtering for personalized recommendations.
Deployed LLMs to generate real-time textual advice based on aggregated financial activity.
Stored data in PostgreSQL with REST API for inter-module communication.
Tested system on dataset of 1000 transactions to evaluate performance.
Combined traditional statistical models with modern AI techniques in hybrid framework.
findings: num: 91.2% classification accuracy achieved with k-NN and decision trees.
num: 6.8% Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) for ARIMA forecasting.
num: 5.4% MAPE for LSTM forecasting outperforming ARIMA.
num: 0.86 F1-score for anomaly detection using autoencoders and Isolation Forest.
LSTM outperformed ARIMA in expense forecasting accuracy.
Hybrid approach combining statistical and AI methods enhances system performance.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper contributes a comprehensive modular architecture for personal finance management that integrates multiple machine learning approaches. It demonstrates the effectiveness of combining traditional statistical methods like ARIMA with deep learning models like LSTM for financial forecasting. The system showcases how Isolation Forests, autoencoders, and SVM can be combined for robust anomaly detection in transaction data. The integration of LLMs for generating personalized financial recommendations represents an advancement in human-AI interaction for financial applications. The hybrid approach provides a framework for building adaptive financial systems that combine analytical precision with personalization.
directly_justifies: Combining k-NN and decision trees achieves 91.2% classification accuracy for transactions.
LSTM forecasting achieves 5.4% MAPE outperforming ARIMA's 6.8% MAPE.
Autoencoders combined with Isolation Forest achieve 0.86 F1-score for anomaly detection.
Recommendation precision reaches 0.89 using matrix factorization and collaborative filtering.
LLM integration provides real-time textual advice based on aggregated financial activity.

Privacy and security aspects beyond OAuth2 not discussed.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: All topic domains were systematically scanned. The paper directly addresses anomaly detection (8.A, 8.B) and predictive modeling (6.A, 6.B) as core components, earning high relevance. Budget recommendation (7.B) and expense categorization (3.A) are implemented but secondary, earning medium relevance. The landscape discussion (4.A) provides context. Mobile UX (9.B) was considered but rejected as the paper mentions mobile interface without detailed design. Data privacy (10.A) was considered but only OAuth2 is mentioned. Financial behavioral profiles (5.A) were considered but not a primary focus. The paper primarily covers anomaly detection, forecasting, and recommendation generation in personal finance systems.
